Crypto counts as confirmed only once the gateway reports the required confirmations. Manual gateways (bank, Wise) keep staff review (approve/reject). hold_hours (whole hours, the console field) can only lengthen the wait: on an automatic gateway a value above 0 holds the payment that many hours instead of 10 minutes; on a manual gateway it is the review window after which the dashboard flags the payment.

extra.conflict: A merchant's fixed custom price stays fixed when the supplier raises its price (the Dhru behaviour a merchant pointed out). The floor used services.cost, which changes only when the admin imports changed items (M96), so orders could be sold below the new supplier cost until then.
extra.decision: User decision (2026-10-31). (1) Effective cost at order time = max(services.cost, the latest synced cost of the service's first active supplier link, credit x credit_rate in USD); floor = effective cost + minimum profit (RULES services 1); an order pays max(resolved price, floor) as before, so a fixed client or group price can no longer sell below a raised supplier cost. The supplier sync updates it at once; importing changed items stays as it is (it updates services.cost and keeps cost_was). (2) Dashboard: services_below_floor uses the effective cost, so a supplier price rise shows right after the sync. (3) Price lists show the real price: Dhru imeiservicelist/serverservicelist/fileservicelist, the REST v1 catalog, the portal catalog and the price export resolve with the effective floor; a sync that changes an effective cost bumps the catalog price version (decision 022). (4) Price-change guard on merchant orders (Dhru, REST v1, portal): the backend keeps, per merchant and service, the last price it listed to them (with currency and time; written only when it changes). If the charged price exceeds that listed price by more than the setting pricing.price_change_tolerance_percent (default 10), the order is refused: 409 PRICE_CHANGED (problem+json with listedPrice and currentPrice) or, on the Dhru surface, ERROR "Price changed. Please refresh the service list and order again.". Up to the tolerance the new price is charged and the order's pricing_snapshot records listedPrice and raised = true with the reason (floor or price change). No listing on record: no check. (5) Notifications: when the resolved price of a service changes for a merchant who placed an order for it in the last 30 days, the merchant gets one digest per change batch (service, old and new price) by email and Telegram (their notification preferences) and the outgoing webhook event service.price_changed (a backend addition to the map's three events: route parity allows it under this B-entry). (6) Lead default, not part of the user's rule: dispatch never fails over to a supplier link whose cost is above the order's charged price; such an order goes to needs_attention. This applies to automatic failover only; a staff change-supplier or dispatch may use a costlier link (recorded as costAbovePrice, resolution orders-suppliers-12). Features: 4b (resolver, listed-price memory, guard, snapshot, setting), 6 (sync recomputes the effective cost, failover check), 7a (Dhru message, listing memory on every list action), 7b (service.price_changed), 9 (dashboard alert), 12a (template and digest job).

extra.decision: User decision (2026-11-01): the accounts are opened in the same DB transaction that creates the merchant. Feature 3 owns the public service `MerchantAccounts.open(tx, { clientId, currency: 'USD', creditLimit, overdraftAllowed })`, exported from src/modules/money/index.ts: raw inserts with ON CONFLICT (ledger_accounts_identity_uq) DO NOTHING of client_wallet (owner_type 'client', overdraft_limit = creditLimit ?? '0.0000') and client_hold (overdraft_limit 0); no postTransaction and no money event; it applies user rule 2 (creditLimit > 0 needs a group with overdraft_allowed, else 422 on creditLimit, the same answer as PATCH /admin/clients/:id/credit-limit) and returns the wallet view {balance '0.0000', reserved '0.0000', creditLimit, available}. POST /admin/clients (2a) calls it with the entered creditLimit; POST /client/auth/register (2b) calls it with creditLimit 0, so no merchant exists without accounts. 'Created on first use' stays only as a safety fallback. Order: feature 3 implements and merges first, 2a calls it; feature 3's seed creates the accounts of the demo merchants that 2a seeds. 2a reads the group (exists, kind not b2c_retail, overdraft_allowed) through a read-only ClientGroupDirectory in the catalog module's public index (4a extends it). Group moves keep the invariant: PATCH /admin/clients/:id {groupId} to a group without overdraft is 422 on groupId while the wallet's overdraft_limit is above 0, and in 4a switching a group's overdraft_allowed off is refused while any of its merchants has a limit above 0. A negative creditLimit stays 422 on creditLimit.

extra.decision: auth_tokens.purpose 'invite' with subject_type 'client', a hash only, expiry 1 hour like every one-time token (decisions 010/019). The link is `<PORTAL_BASE_URL>/set-password?token=<token>`, built from the new config key PORTAL_BASE_URL (the counterpart of the console base URL). 2a writes the token and the outbox event `merchant.invited` (ids only, never the token); until feature 12a adds the template, 2b's MailSender development implementation logs a redacted line. The consuming route is POST /client/auth/password/reset {token, password}, which accepts purposes 'reset' and 'invite': it sets password_hash (argon2id), password_changed_at = now and email_verified_at = now (the link proves the email), sets used_at, voids the merchant's other unused tokens and answers 204; it does not sign in. The status stays 'pending' until staff approve with PATCH /admin/clients/:id. A merchant who misses the hour uses POST /client/auth/password/forgot, which also works for a pending merchant with no password yet. auth_tokens.purpose is a closed vocabulary: CHECK auth_tokens_purpose_check purpose IN ('invite','reset','verify_email','magic_link'), from an exported AUTH_TOKEN_PURPOSES const in src/modules/identity/db/schema.ts (STAFF_TOKEN_PURPOSES is derived from it), shipped in the lead's single pre-wave-1 audit migration (0003).

extra.decision: Common rules of the merchant portal routes (ALIGNMENT § 3 and § 7, decision 018). Public routes (register, verify-email, login, password/forgot, password/reset) need no session and no CSRF token but are accepted only with an Origin header that is one of CORS_ORIGINS; pipeline order IP rules (403 IP_NOT_ALLOWED) → per-IP rate limit (429 RATE_LIMITED with Retry-After; login, 2fa and password routes have the strict limits) → handler. Session routes use the cookie gsm_client_session (httpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax, __Host- in production) and the readable CSRF cookie csrf_token_client; every mutation with a session sends X-CSRF-Token (403 CSRF_FAILED, never signs out); no active session is 401 UNAUTHORIZED. A sign-in creates a pending session (sessions.stage pending_totp, 10 minutes) when a second step is needed and an active one otherwise; reaching active rotates the token; lifetimes are the settings sessions.client_* (30 days absolute, 10080 minutes idle by default). Session-ending codes (401, 403 ACCOUNT_SUSPENDED, 403 IP_NOT_ALLOWED) are only ever about the caller, so a wrong current password or code is 422 on its field, never 401. Success statuses: one per route, bodies JSON or empty; lists are simple-rest. Cache-Control: no-store on /client/auth/* and on any response that carries a secret. Passwords follow the staff policy (at least 10 characters, not trivial: 422 WEAK_PASSWORD). One-time tokens (verify_email, reset, invite) are 1 hour, single use, hash only (decisions 010/019). Mails are outbox events with ids only (merchant.email_verification, merchant.password_reset, merchant.invited); 2b registers the processor that hands them to the MailSender interface. Merchant 2FA is optional TOTP (6 digits, plus or minus one step, a used step is never accepted twice: clients.totp_last_step), with clients.twofa_enabled false while the secret is only pending; the columns these specs need on clients (twofa_enabled, totp_last_step, password_changed_at) come with 2b's migration and a B116 note.

An existing email changes nothing and sends nothing. extra.decision: Lead record (feature 16). Pay is idempotent per checkout session and Idempotency-Key: payments gain checkout_session_id, idempotency_key, checkout_url and request_fingerprint (migration 0017_b2c_payments, schema additions); the same key with another gateway or return URL is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED, a first request still running is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS (a stale one restarts after 60 s), and a start whose guarded update misses is 409 INVALID_TRANSITION. A gateway confirmation captures the payment even when it was already failed (an expired crypto payment confirmed late takes money, so it must end in an order or a refund). A second payment for one checkout is a duplicate: booked and refunded at once, never the order's payment, no receipt invoice. The order's payment is the one the approved refund names, else the one linked to the order's first receipt invoice. The receipt is rendered once after the capture commits (outbox event receipt.render on the files queue) and stored; downloads serve the stored bytes and render on the fly only when the stored copy is missing; the route lists 503 UNAVAILABLE. Refunds stay processing between the approval and the gateway's answer (user rule 7); the gateway call runs outside any transaction with the key refund-<id>, and refund-<id>-<n> once the gateway refused it for good (n = refunds.send_attempt, a schema addition with CHECK >= 1; a 4xx other than 408, 409, 425 and 429 fails the refund, a timeout or 5xx retries with the same key); a late refund.failed of an older attempt is logged and ignored (the attempt travels as gateway metadata), a late refund.succeeded still completes. A failed refund still counts against what is left on the payment until it is retried; approving with nothing left is 422 'Nothing is left to refund on this payment.'; approval locks the order, then the payment, then the refund. The storefront policy autoRefundFailed (default on) covers only rejections the system decides (a supplier's result): a staff rejection refunds at once, and with the policy off a system rejection opens a refund requested by the system (no journal) whose approval posts from customer funds. DisputeLedger alone posts b2c_chargeback (key dispute:<id>:chargeback) whether the accept or the gateway's lost comes first; a win posts nothing and returns the payment to the status its completed refunds leave; the blocklist and risk level after a chargeback are feature 18's. openQuestions.answer: Cumulative completed-order spend in USD since account creation; the admin sets earn_threshold per group in the console; a nightly job promotes automatically and never demotes; the admin can change a merchant's group by hand at any time.

openQuestions.topic: Fixed custom prices when the supplier cost rises
openQuestions.question: A merchant's custom price is fixed; when the supplier raises its price, how do we avoid selling below cost without overcharging the merchant silently? (raised by the user from a merchant conversation)
openQuestions.default: Order-time floor = cost + minimum profit on services.cost only (it changes when the admin imports the supplier's changed items).
openQuestions.answer: Floor uses max(service cost, latest synced supplier price); dashboard alert; the real price in imeiservicelist; import unchanged. An order whose price is more than a configurable tolerance (default 10%) above the merchant's last listed price is refused with PRICE_CHANGED (Dhru message: refresh the service list); within the tolerance the new price is charged and the order records the raise. Merchants who used a service in the last 30 days are notified (email, Telegram, webhook) when its price changes. Full rule: MISMATCHES B117.
